reason: E1 supports the existence of a strength plateau in the specific alloy, and E2/E3 support edge-dislocation-dominated deformation in related BCC refractory HEAs, but no cited evidence supports the specific mechanism of thermal super-jogging or the claim that compositional tweaks alter dislocation core energies in this system.
premises: NbTaHfTiZrV₀.₅ exhibits a high-temperature strength plateau between ~673 K and 1073 K
The deformation mode in BCC refractory HEAs can transition from screw-dislocation-dominated to edge-dislocation-dominated at elevated temperatures
Thermal activation enables super-jogging in edge dislocations, which act as strong barriers to slip
Edge dislocation mobility governs the strength plateau in this alloy system
Minor compositional changes can alter dislocation core energies and thus edge dislocation mobility
